readback.name: Poincare.DeTurckChartLift.exists_actual_metric_variation
readback.mathematical_statement:
Let M be a Hausdorff smooth manifold modeled on E = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3), with the boundaryless model closedSmoothModelWithCorners 3. Let g0 be an actual smooth Riemannian metric on its tangent bundle, anchor a point of M, and F : E → Bilin a globally smooth map into the existing continuous bilinear forms E →L[ℝ] E →L[ℝ] ℝ. Assume F has compact support, its topological support lies in the actual target of extChartAt I anchor, and each F z is symmetric.

There exists one real ε > 0 and a total family gt : ℝ → ClosedSmoothRiemannianMetric 3 M such that gt 0 = g0 as metric objects. Every gt s is a symmetric positive definite smooth tangent-bundle metric, with the bounded-unit-ball condition of ContMDiffRiemannianMetric in the existing fiber topology. For every signed real s with |s| < ε, simultaneously for every x : M, the actual fiber bilinear form satisfies (gt s).inner x = g0.inner x + s • chartLift anchor F x.

The chartLift here is the pinned actual tensor. Inside the genuine preferred-chart source, it evaluates F at the forward chart coordinate and precomposes both tensor slots with mfderiv I 𝓘(ℝ,E) of the forward chart at x. Outside that source it is zero. It is not an arbitrary supplied section or a replacement coordinate tensor.

For the same ε and every such s, at every z in the entire genuine preferred-chart target, CovariantDerivative.chartMetric of (gt s).inner equals chartMetric of g0.inner plus s • F z as continuous bilinear forms. The pinned chartMetric pulls the metric back through mfderivWithin of the inverse chart on Set.range I. The equality includes target points outside the support of F and uses the actual forward and inverse chart differentials.

The ε precedes all signed parameters, manifold points and target coordinates. No positivity margin, candidate perturbed metric, smooth chartLift, forward/inverse differential identity, coordinate recovery identity or modified norm is supplied as a hypothesis. Compactness, connectedness and second countability of M are not hypotheses. Smoothness of each metric concerns its base point x; the type requires no continuity or smoothness of s ↦ gt s, and no flow equation or flow existence. The affine constraints apply only when |s| < ε; the codomain still requires actual smooth Riemannian metrics for every real s.
